text:
Raja P.: Heads-up — after the 1.4.3 canary rollout we're seeing a ~30% drop in tokens/sec for low-batch (batch=1/2) requests to llama2-13b on G4dn.
Lina G.: ugh. saw any CI flags?
perf-ci: CI perf/job-llama2-13b (canary) failed: median tokens/sec 420 -> 290 (regression +31%). Link: https://ci.example/5567
Anna M.: any recent merges touching kernel selector or batching heuristics?
Raja P.: suspect: commit 9f3b2e7 (runtime/kernel: dynamic kernel selection path) + 3a7d4c1 (batching: prefer packable batches) merged this morning. Both touch hot paths.
Sasha K.: quick profile from the canary nodes shows CPU time up in "pack_batches" and a 2x increase in memcpy for kv_cache refill. paste: ```
# top hotloops
pack_batches  34.2%
select_kernels 12.8%
kv_cache::refill_memcpy 18.7%
```
Lina G.: can we bisect to confirm which commit caused the regression? ci perf already pointed at the canary commit range.
Raja P.: I'm running a local bisect: `git bisect start HEAD v1.4.2; git bisect run ./tools/perf_check.sh --model=llama2-13b --seq=1024 --batch=1`
Anna M.: if bisect blames 9f3b2e7 then we should revert that on main and cherry-pick the safe parts to a hotfix branch. We shouldn't block customer traffic longer than needed.
perf-ci: bisect result: first-bad: 9f3b2e7. Good: 7a1c8b2.
Sasha K.: confirmed locally — 9f3b2e7 enables an "aggressive kernel swap" which disables the memcpy batching for kv cache refill in some paths; that causes cache thrash + more mem copies for small batches. Patch is well-intentioned for long sequences but regresses short-batch workloads.
Lina G.: plan: cut branch `release/1.4.4-hotfix`, cherry-pick revert commit for 9f3b2e7 (revert-only), and include a small unit test for kv cache path. I'll create PR and request fast-track.
Raja P.: I can validate the revert on canary nodes and run `tools/bench/throughput.py --model llama2-13b --seq 1024 --batch 1 --runs 10` before deploy.
Lina G.: created PR #5879: revert 9f3b2e7 + add kv_cache unit test. CI: run perf job with compare to baseline.
deploy-bot: canary rollback requested by Lina G. — rolling back canary to tag v1.4.2.
perf-ci: compare report attached — revert branch median tokens/sec back to 415 (within noise of baseline 420).
Anna M.: great. once CI green, cherry-pick revert to `release/1.4.4-hotfix` and cut patch. Sasha/Triage: please prepare release notes explaining the regression and mitigation.
Sasha K.: will add details: root cause = kernel selector "aggressive" path that reduced memcpy coalescing, impacted small-batch latency/throughput. Follow-up: refine selector to be sequence-length aware and not flip behavior for batch<=2.
Raja P.: postmortem ticket created: https://proj/RED-2345. Rolling canary back to green now. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Lina G.: assigning QA to run a smoke matrix: batches {1,2,4,8} x seq {256,1024,2048} across G4dn and A100.
perf-ci: perf job for PR #5879 passed and marked as perf-regression-fix.
Anna M.: moving this to release queue. Reminder: include a test in CI perf that runs small-batch throughput checks to catch this class of regressions.
Raja P.: noted. We'll add a small-batch benchmark to the nightly perf suite and alert on >10% drop.
Lina G.: closing loop — hotfix cut, canary reverted, PR merged after perf validation, follow-ups for selector refinement and extra tests. Thanks everyone.
